Vituperate

/vy-TOO-puh-rayt/ - the stress falls on TOO · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Vituperate means to berate; to attack with harsh, abusive language.

Cicero could vituperate with the best of Rome, flaying a rival for an hour while the galleries took notes.

Worked Example

The retired admiral's letters to the editor stopped arguing years ago; now they simply vituperated, page after page of abuse that the paper trimmed to its mildest paragraph.

Vituperate is beyond criticism and past scolding: it is sustained verbal abuse, delivered to wound. An upbraiding (this unit) still has a fault and a lesson at its center; vituperation has only the target. Even a scathing review keeps its composure — vituperation has thrown composure away.

How Vituperate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

revile

revile: to heap open scorn on someone

lambaste

lambaste: to thrash someone in words, publicly

Antonyms

laud

laud: to praise in formal, admiring terms

applaud

applaud: to voice warm approval

How Strong Is It? — criticize → lambaste → vituperate

criticize vs. vituperate

criticize vs. vituperate: Criticize is far milder than vituperate — it can be fair, careful, even kind.

lambaste vs. vituperate

lambaste vs. vituperate: Lambaste stops just short of vituperate: a lambasting is a hard public thrashing, but vituperation settles into sustained, naked abuse.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — vituper

Root — vituper: fault-finding (Latin vitium, fault + parare, to supply)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: verb-forming ending

Put it together

Put it together: Vituper- (from vitium, 'fault, defect,' + parare, 'to supply') + -ate = to serve up faults. Latin vituperare was to find and dress every defect in a person; English kept the industrial scale — to vituperate is to supply someone's faults to them in bulk, loudly.

Use the root in a new word: vitiate

Use the root in a new word: vitiate: One tainted sample can vitiate a whole study — the same vitium, a single fault spoiling the lot.

Word Choice

formal / literary

Vituperate is the heaviest artillery in this unit's scolding arsenal: sustained, abusive, meant to wound. Upbraid still teaches; scathing still aims; vituperation just batters. Its noun is vituperation, its adjective vituperative — all best reserved for abuse worth documenting.
